Okay, so today we continue the topic of secret societies. Last class, we discussed how they come into power. Today, we will look at where they come from and what they believe.

To understand secret societies, I first need to explain to you the history of religion in the western world. In the western world, there have been three major stages of religious development: the mother goddess civilization, polytheism, and monotheism. Polytheism means believing in many gods, while monotheism means believing that only one god exists.

The mother goddess civilization came about because of agriculture. In an agricultural world, you face two problems: ensuring your crops are healthy and harvested on time, and having as many children as possible to work the fields. A religion developed to address both issues, known as the mother goddess civilization.

At the center of this religion is the womb—considered a divine portal from the spirit world into our world. The woman's womb is central to this belief system, and women hold significant control because everything in this world is interconnected, harmonized, and balanced.

The stars also play a role, leading to astrology—the study of star movements to understand their impact on our world. In an ideal scenario, the stars indicate when to plant crops and have children, maintaining the high status of women as direct representatives of the mother goddess who rules the world. The mother goddess is often represented as a bird because birds dominate the sky, and life comes from above.

The mother goddess civilization also features symbols like bowls—representing fertility and energy. Sex in this society is communal, with rituals called fertility cults where multiple men can have sex with one woman to ensure the best possible genetic outcomes.

With population growth and resource struggle due to war, we transitioned to polytheism. War introduced the concept of property, leading to hierarchies, marriage, and a decrease in women's roles while increasing men's. Different societies developed gods to motivate soldiers during conflicts.
